timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 太宗第三子，早年历封韩王、襄王、寿王。
timeline.summary_en: Third son of Taizong, earlier enfeoffed as Prince of Han, Xiang, and Shou.

timeline.title: 即位
timeline.summary: 太宗崩，恒即位，改元咸平。
timeline.summary_en: Succeeded upon Taizong's death, changing the era to Xianping.

timeline.title: 澶渊之盟
timeline.summary: 辽军南下，寇准促亲征，订澶渊盟约：宋辽约为兄弟，岁币银绢；此后百年无大战。
timeline.summary_en: When Liao marched south, Kou Zhun urged him to campaign in person; the Chanyuan Treaty made the two states brothers with annual tribute, keeping peace for a century.

timeline.title: 天书封禅
timeline.summary: 伪造天书，东封泰山，礼制开支浩繁，为后世讥议。
timeline.summary_en: He fabricated a heavenly letter and performed the Fengshan rites on Mount Tai; the lavish ceremonies drew later censure.

timeline.title: 真宗崩
timeline.summary_en: Died; succeeded by Renzong under Empress Liu's regency.

timeline.title: 真宗总评
timeline.summary: 澶渊定局而天书封禅耗财，晚年朝政日弛。
timeline.summary_en: The Chanyuan settlement stabilized the north, but the heavenly-letter deification drained the treasury and relaxed governance.

bio_md:
# 宋真宗 · 主要事迹

赵恒为[[n-song-tai-zong|宋太宗]]第三子，至道三年（997）即位，改元咸平。继位初期任用李沆、王旦等，号称贤相辈出，「咸平之治」为史家所称。

景德元年（1004）辽军大举南下，宰相寇准力促亲征，真宗渡河驻澶州，宋辽订「澶渊之盟」：约为兄弟之国，宋岁输银绢三十万。盟约以岁币买来百年和平，边境自此息兵，然岁币之制亦为后世争论。

后期真宗倦于政事，大中祥符元年（1008）伪造天书、东封泰山，封禅祠祀之费浩繁，朝政由是渐弛，史家多以「澶渊定局而后天书耗财」论其得失。

乾兴元年（1022）真宗崩，太子赵祯即位，刘太后临朝，是为[[n-song-ren|仁宗]]。

bio_parts_en.value:
, took the throne in 997 and changed the era to Xianping. His early years were served by chancellors Li Hang and Wang Dan; historians speak of a "Xianping golden age."

In 1004 Liao marched south in force. Chancellor Kou Zhun pressed the emperor to campaign in person; Zhenzong crossed the river to Chanzhou and concluded the Chanyuan Treaty: the two states became brothers, with Song paying an annual tribute of silver and silk. The treaty bought a century of peace, though the tribute system remained contested by later historians.

In his later years Zhenzong wearied of rule. In 1008 he fabricated a heavenly letter and performed the Fengshan sacrifices on Mount Tai; the lavish rites drained the treasury and governance slackened - summed up by historians as "Chanyuan settled, then the heavenly letter squandered."
